summary: HTTPS is live on node1:8443 with automatic certificate renewal, zero-downtime nginx reloads, and verified persistence across a full node reboot.
actions_performed: Installed Ubuntu Noble’s nginx 1.24 package without upgrading the existing OS or kernel.
Configured HTTPS on IPv4 and IPv6 port 8443.
Created a 30-day certificate renewal script with a seven-day pre-expiry threshold.
Enabled a persistent daily systemd renewal timer.
Demonstrated certificate rotation while 250 consecutive HTTPS requests completed successfully.
Rebooted node1 once and verified complete recovery.

evidence.requirement: Preserve the installed OS release and kernel; use compatible software
evidence.summary: Ubuntu 24.04.3 and kernel 6.8.0-71 were retained. Distribution nginx 1.24 was installed with zero existing packages upgraded.
Nginx configuration passed validation, listened on 0.0.0.0:8443 and [::]:8443, and returned the expected content over HTTPS at the managed node IP.

evidence.requirement: Renew the certificate automatically before expiry
evidence.summary: The enabled persistent daily timer invokes a seven-day-threshold renewal service. A served one-day certificate was automatically replaced by a new 30-day certificate with a different serial.

evidence.requirement: Pick up each new certificate while continuing to answer requests
evidence.summary: Nginx served the new certificate after reload; 250 of 250 HTTPS requests succeeded during the exercised rotation, with zero failures.

Before reboot, boot ID f9bf293d-1eb8-423e-b185-84e94db646f3 had healthy HTTPS and timer state. The safe reboot was acknowledged and the connection reset. Afterward, boot ID changed to 2780af21-4c99-4955-8537-18b7e13542a7; nginx and the renewal timer were enabled and active, port 8443 was listening, the same certificate and HTTPS data were recovered, and nginx configuration remained valid.
